summary: Graceful overflow: model-pin overflow causing instantaneous 429s and request drop without fallback
description: Issue summary: Beacon Health is seeing immediate 429 responses when a pinned model route exceeds capacity. Instead of being routed to a fallback model variant or queued briefly, requests are rejected and surface to the application. Impact: client-facing health-app backend receives 429s for ~30s during daily morning spike (03:42-03:46 UTC) causing degraded UX and error alerts. Timeline: 2026-03-12 03:42 UTC - first surge; 03:43-03:46 - sustained 429s; 03:46 - partial recovery once queued tokens cleared. Observed behavior: requests to route /v1/generate pinned to redwood-llama-70b-v2 are immediately answered with 429 and X-RateLimit-* headers show per-route bucket exhausted; fallback rules exist in their console but appear not to trigger. Expected behavior: seamless overflow to pre-configured fallback (rlhf-quant-8bit) or short queueing/spillover policy instead of hard 429 during short warmup of fallback pool. Customer asks for explanation of why fallback did not trigger, and configuration guidance to allow transient overflow without large billing spikes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated pool with route pinned to redwood-llama-70b-v2, configure fallback route to rlhf-quant-8bit (console: Routes > Edit > Fallback) but leave fallback weight default
2) Send 150 parallel short requests (avg 120 tokens) to /v1/generate from a single API key over 30s to emulate morning fanout
3) Observe immediate 429s for a subset of requests; check response headers for X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset
4) Watch dedicated-autoscaler and fallback pool metrics in console; fallback pool shows cold start and then scales but after initial 429 window
investigation_notes: Initial triage: per-route token bucket consumed rapidly due to many parallel short requests; console fallback was configured but route-level pin appears to block normal fallback path (design: exact-pins avoid automatic spillover to preserve determinism for enterprise customers)
Autoscaler behavior: fallback pool cold-start latency ~35-45s in us-east observed in metrics; autoscaler does not preemptively warm a fallback if pinned route is considered authoritative

Quota accounting: requests counted against route token bucket before routing policy evaluation in current config; when bucket is zero the request is rejected instead of being forwarded to fallback or queued
Hypothesis: policy combination 'model pin + strict per-route quota' leads to hard 429; customer expected 'graceful spillover' but pin semantics intentionally prioritize strict routing
Risk note: enabling transparent spillover can increase footprint on fallback pool and lead to unexpected billing; recommend rate-limited spillover with token-weight cap
resolution: Short-term workaround (applied): temporarily increase route token quota for pinned route and enable short-lived burst credits in console (Routes > Quotas > Burst window + extra tokens) to absorb morning spike
- Configure a controlled fallback policy: Console -> Routes -> Edit routing policy -> set 'Fallback mode' to 'allowed-with-rate-limit' and specify token ceiling (e.g., 10k tokens/min)
- Enable 'pre-warm fallback' for critical routes: set fallback pool min-replicas=1 during known daily windows to reduce cold-start 35s overhead
- Use token-weighted spillover so requests get forwarded only if per-request token estimate <= spillover_threshold
Operational guidance: add a canary policy that routes 2% of requests to fallback during quiet hours to keep cache/weights warm without large cost impact
Follow-ups: SRE to propose UI change for clearer pin+fallback semantics; Engineering to evaluate route evaluation order (quota vs fallback) for possible safe reorder
Customer communicated acceptance of temporary quota bump; ticket to remain open for config follow-up
